Q: What is the recommended frontend approach for beginners using Django? A:

Plain JavaScript first.

  • AJAX isn’t a separate choice (it’s just async requests done in JS), and jQuery is largely legacy.
  • Modern vanilla JavaScript works well with Django templates, has a gentler learning curve today, and gives the best long-term foundation.

keep the frontend simple at first. Learn Django templates, HTML/CSS, and basic JS before adding libraries or frameworks.

Avoid over-engineering early, most Django apps don’t need a heavy frontend stack to start with.

Q: Dealing with colons in paths stored inside a text file A:

To offer a more concise and better-performing alternative to your own answer; it works irrespective of whether the paths in the file are (possibly selectively) double-quoted:

$read_paths =
  (Get-Content -ReadCount 0 $pathToFile) -notmatch '^\s*(#|$)' -replace '"'

  • For brevity, $pathToFile is passed positionally to Get-Content's -Path parameter; if it contains a literal file path that happens to contain [ or ] characters, you'd have to target the -LiteralPath parameter explicitly (Get-Content -ReadCount 0 -LiteralPath $pathToFile).

  • Using -ReadCount 0 with Get-Content is a performance optimization that reads all lines from the file into an array of strings at once, as a single operation (rather than streaming the lines, one by one), which not only speeds up reading considerably, but secondarily also ensures that an array is returned even if the input file happens to contain just one line (without -ReadCount 0, you'd have to use @(...), the array-subexpression operator to ensure that).

  • Using -notmatch, the negated regular-expression matching operator and -replace, the regular-expression-based string replacement operator on an array as the input (the LHS) ensures that the operation is performed on each element, which is a feature that is common to PowerShell's comparison operators:

    • -notmatch '^\s*(#|$)' filters out any lines that are:

      • empty
      • blank (all-whitespace)
      • start with #, possibly preceded by whitespace.

    • -replace '"' effectively removes all " chars. from each input string (this should be good enough in the case at hand, given that file paths themselves cannot contain " characters on Windows).

Q: Unable to retrieve project metadata. Ensure it's an MSBuild-based .NET Core project. (Migrations) A:

I ran into this again in 2026 and this time the reason was a drifting dotnet-ef version to my project's dotnet version. So my project is dotnet7 and dotnet ef --version showed me v10.

So seemingly dotnet-ef is not super compatible between dotnet versions but you can freeze it for your project.

dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install dotnet-ef --version 7.0.20
dotnet tool restore

For the right version check https://www.nuget.org/packages/dotnet-ef and select the versions tab and take the highest version of your dotnet version.

Also make sure you use the right type of / (see my first answer) and that you are in the right folder and paths are correct.

Q: Convert WEBP images to PNG by Linux command A:

How to convert .webp images to .png on Linux

Tested on Linux Ubuntu 20.04

This question is the top hit for the Google search of "linux convert .webp image to png". Therefore, for anyone stumbling here and just wanting that simple answer, here it is:

# 1. Install the `webp` tool
sudo apt update
sudo apt install webp

# 2. Use it to convert in.webp to out.png
dwebp in.webp -o out.png

Done! You now have out.png.
